html:
The Danish West Indies were the Caribbean colony of Denmark, on the islands of St. Thomas, St. John and St. Croix in the Virgin Islands. The map shows it in 1715, when Denmark held St. Thomas.

The Danish West India Company settled St. Thomas in 1672, took St. John in 1718 and bought St. Croix from France in 1733. The islands grew sugar with enslaved Africans brought by the Atlantic slave trade, and the harbour of Charlotte Amalie on St. Thomas became a busy free port. In 1733 enslaved people on St. John rose and held the island for months.

Denmark banned its slave trade in a law of 1792 that took effect in 1803. In 1848 a revolt on St. Croix pushed the governor to declare all slaves free. In 1917 Denmark sold the islands to the United States, which wanted them as a naval base during the First World War. They are now the US Virgin Islands.
